Explain how the FBS score is calculated for packaged foods
Why does Quaker Oats have an FBS score of 10.0?
cases.expectedFactualValue: Base 6.0 + 1.0 (Whole food base) + 0.5 (Nutrient density) + 1.5 (Fibre) + 1.0 (Protein) - 0.0 (Sugar) = 10.0 Excellent

cases.query: Why is Maggi 2-Minute Noodles FBS score 5.6?
cases.expectedFactualValue: High sodium (980mg per 100g) and saturated fat (7.5g) penalize baseline score despite 8.5g protein

cases.query: Why does Campa Cola have a low FBS score of 2.7?
cases.expectedFactualValue: Sugary beverage penalty (-2.5 pts) applied due to 10.8g added sugar with near-zero protein and fibre

cases.query: Why does Parle-G have an FBS score of 4.3?
cases.expectedFactualValue: Refined sugar (25g per 100g) and palm oil saturated fat (6.2g) lower score into Limited band

cases.query: Why is Britannia Good Day Butter Cookies rated Limited with 3.9?
cases.expectedFactualValue: 11g saturated fat and 22g added sugar cause strong penalties in FBS algorithm

cases.query: What factors explain Amul Taaza Milk's 7.5 FBS score?
cases.expectedFactualValue: Pure whole food base (+1.0), protein contribution (+0.32), zero added sugar, low sodium (50mg)

cases.query: What penalties apply to industrial food additives in FBS?
cases.expectedFactualValue: Products containing 5 or more industrial additives receive a -0.7 point ultra-processing deduction

cases.query: How does trans fat affect the Food Benefit Score?
cases.expectedFactualValue: Trans fat exceeding 0.2g per 100g triggers an automatic -0.5 point penalty

cases.query: What is the baseline starting score in the FBS formula?
cases.expectedFactualValue: Every packaged food begins at a standard baseline of 6.0 points

cases.query: What are the 6 official FBS score bands?
cases.expectedFactualValue: Excellent (9.0-10.0), Very Good (8.0-8.9), Good (7.0-7.9), Moderate (5.0-6.9), Limited (3.0-4.9), Poor (1.0-2.9)

cases.query: Why is a product's FBS score marked as Pending?
cases.expectedFactualValue: When a manufacturer fails to disclose one of the 5 mandatory nutrients (Energy, Protein, Sugar, Fat, Sodium)
